extracted.intended_audience: Army commanders, public affairs officers (PAOs), and Army public affairs staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for Army public affairs activities, including requirements for releasing information, supporting public events, producing PA publications, web content management, and election-year restrictions. Intended to instruct commanders and PA personnel how to evaluate and approve PA actions and products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicize Army global missions/campaign plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Give adequate publicity throughout the year to the global missions of the Army and the Army campaign plan, as directed by the CSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and approve support requests at lowest practical command level
rubrics_metrics.description: Process and approve requests for Army support at the lowest practical command level and forward all requests requiring DA or DOD approval through command channels to the OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward requests for high-profile events ≥45 days prior
rubrics_metrics.description: Forward requests for approval of support to events which could be of national or international interest through command channels to the OCPA not later than 45 days prior to the event or immediately if within 45 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Route foreign support requests via Defense Attaché Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Forward requests for support from foreign countries through the proper U.S. Defense Attaché Office to the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense (Public Affairs) (OASD (PA)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum disclosure/minimum delay for unclassified information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide unclassified information about the Army and its activities to the public with maximum disclosure and minimum delay while not releasing information that would adversely affect national security or threaten personal safety or privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance transparency with national security and privacy protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release unfavorable news with same care and speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Release unfavorable news with the same care and speed as favorable news; be candid when dealing with the American people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of information provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that all information provided to internal or external audiences is accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take steps to verify facts before release; correct errors promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct erroneous public information
rubrics_metrics.description: Take appropriate action to correct erroneous information about the Army that appears in any medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively pursue corrections when incorrect Army-related information is published or broadcast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid promotional/self‑serving releases and staged events
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid promotional, self-serving releases and events staged solely for publicity purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA resources should not be used for publicity stunts or purely promotional activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect classified information per AR 380–5
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect information classified in the interest of national security under AR 380–5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not release classified material; follow security classification rules and consult security authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise commanders on PA needs
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs at ACOM level and below will advise commanders regarding the PA needs of the command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop PA plans and programs
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs will develop public affairs plans and programs for their commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assist with command messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist in formulating and releasing command messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide drafting, review, and coordination support for official messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison to higher‑headquarters PAO and planning cells
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve as a liaison between the commander and the next higher headquarters PAO; provide coordination and representation to planning, coordinating, and operations cells as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervise production/distribution of PA information
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervise the preparation, production, and distribution of printed and electronic PA information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure quality control and adherence to approval processes for PA materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support acquisition of print/visual information products
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist in the development and acquisition of print and visual information products in support of PA programs used on installation command channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with appropriate offices (e.g., printing control) and ensure rights/fees are settled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise commander on audience attitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: Advise the commander on audience attitudes and perceptions of policies, programs, and information needs, using surveys or focus groups as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use research (surveys, focus groups, informal feedback) and coordinate with other staff (DOIM, Resource Management) for support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct PA assistance visits to units
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct regular assistance visits to command units to assess PA programs and determine unit commanders’ needs for support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide training and support to UPARs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide training and support to the command-designated unit public affairs representatives (UPARs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain desktop publishing capability with DOIM
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate with installation DOIM to maintain a desktop publishing capability dedicated to the PA office (applies to PAOs responsible for publications authorized by this regulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate on‑post distribution of non‑DOD commercial publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist in coordinating on-post distribution of non-DOD commercial publications as defined in AR 210–7 and paragraph 3–8a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop materials to meet special PA needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop materials and products to meet the command’s special public affairs needs (applies to commands subordinate to HQDA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated PAO authority for release of official information
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve as the commander’s designated review and approval authority for the release of official information to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAO must ensure coordination and approvals prior to public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command Web content manager responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve as the command Web content manager: review and release official information intended for the public World Wide Web and command Web sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow content approval process and DOD web policy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure web content approval and OPSEC/SJA coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure Web content providers have followed the content approval process, including coordination with the command’s OPSEC officer, security manager, and staff judge advocate, if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate legal/security reviews before public posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execute information‑assurance and web‑risk responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Execute information-assurance and Web-risk assessment responsibilities as required by AR 25–1 and AR 25–2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly review of publicly accessible web sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct routine quarterly reviews of publicly accessible Web sites to ensure compliance with AR 25–1 policies and that content remains relevant and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑posting approval of new web content
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to posting, approve for release new content posted on the command Web site in accordance with DOD Web policy and referenced AR paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow DOD/DA web posting approval and coordination steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult PAO and prepublication review for releases by Army personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual governed by this regulation who intends to release information to the public must consult with a PAO and, if applicable, submit material in its intended release form for prepublication review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retired personnel, former employees, and nonactive reservists must use the security review process to avoid compromising national security.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA activities and event access based on law and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for planning and conducting PA activities and evaluating access to facilities are based on public law, executive order, DOD directives/instructions, DA regulations, and practical experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow applicable laws, DOD/DA rules, and use common sense and good taste (5 CFR 2635 and DOD 5500.7–R referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑discrimination in event admission/seating
rubrics_metrics.description: Army participation in public events may be authorized only if admission, seating, and other accommodations are available to all without regard to sex, race, creed, color, sexual preference, or national origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Army resources only for common interest/benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Army resources will be used only to support events and activities of common interest and benefit to local, state, regional, national, or broadly represented audiences; commanders must give equal consideration and support to comparable events/organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational constraints may preclude responding to every valid request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event scale definitions (local/regional/national)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines local (single community/command sphere), regional (more than one state), and national (US-wide) events and audiences for evaluation purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use definitions when determining scope and appropriateness of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on PA resources for psychological/deception operations
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs and their staffs will not initiate or conduct psychological or deception operations and will not permit PA resources to be used to support such activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event support must primarily/mutually benefit the DA and meet conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Support to public events must primarily or mutually benefit the Department of the Army and conform to conditions: (1) not interfere with official duty or readiness; (2) no additional fee may be charged specifically to observe Army participation (general admission may be acceptable if incidental); (3) other statutes/regulations must not restrict participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult DOD 5500.7–R and AR 600–29 for fund-raising/membership-drive constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of commercial products requires rights/fees and consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders may use commercial products if all fees are paid and rights to use the product obtained; consult PAO, local SJA, and printing control officer when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy exception request timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy exception requests are forwarded through channels to the OCPA policy division not later than 45 days prior to the required date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective benefit prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Army participation must not selectively benefit (or appear to benefit) any person, group, corporation, religion/sect, fraternal or political organization, or commercial venture; providers of support to non-Federal entities must be willing to provide equal support to comparable events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid endorsement of individuals/organizations/campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: PA activities will not support any event involving (or appearing to involve) promotion, endorsement, or sponsorship of any individual, civilian enterprise, religious/sectarian movement, ideological movement, organization, or political campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lending Army equipment, personnel, or logistical support cannot involve or appear to involve endorsement. Exceptions allow nonpartisan government, school, civic, veterans, or recognized public-service organizations and certain community‑benefit uses of narrow‑membership facilities when benefit accrues to community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for supporting religious facilities/events
rubrics_metrics.description: Army support of community activities conducted in religious facilities may be authorized if: (1) the program is community-wide, nonsectarian, and of common interest/benefit; and (2) the program is broadly publicized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a house of worship as a site is permitted when the activity is not part of a religious service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support to veterans organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in events sponsored by veterans organizations may be authorized when such participation supports programs oriented to the veteran rather than sectarian/fraternal/national-origin aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support to nonpublic school activities criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Support to nonpublic school activities may be authorized when participation is clearly educational, patriotic, or in support of Army recruiting programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsoring organization nature: chief beneficiary test
rubrics_metrics.description: Army participation in events sponsored by organizations with a narrow membership base may be supported if (1) the chief beneficiary is the community at large rather than the organization and (2) participation does not produce a special interest or benefit to the sponsoring organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: industry-wide association conventions may qualify; a meeting of a single business would not.

rubrics_metrics.name: No support for organizations that restrict access to organizational data
rubrics_metrics.description: Community relations support is not authorized for events sponsored by organizations whose constitution, bylaws, membership qualifications, or ritual are withheld from the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army role in event must be incidental
rubrics_metrics.description: Army participation must be incidental to the event except for patriotic programs or national holiday celebrations, which must be open to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited uses of Army personnel at off‑installation public events
rubrics_metrics.description: Army personnel will not be used as ushers, bag handlers, guards, escorts at beauty pageants, messengers, parking attendants, or in similar demeaning/inappropriate capacities during public events conducted off military installations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruiting potential considered in participation evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruiting potential will be weighed when evaluating requests for Army participation; regulation applies to activities undertaken in direct or indirect support of recruiting whether initiated by DA elements or civilian community.

rubrics_metrics.name: No participation in events primarily for commercial benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Army participation is not authorized for events clearly designed or conducted primarily for commercial benefit (to stimulate sales or increase business). Exception: participation may be authorized in direct support of Army recruiting in malls/shopping centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not compete with available commercial resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Army personnel, equipment, transportation, or other resources will not be provided to civilian-sponsored activities if commercial resources/services in the public domain could reasonably provide such support; documented waivers by unions/CEs may permit support but all other regulation stipulations still apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of Army resources includes communications equipment, transportation, visual information support, ambulances, PA systems, food equipment, bleachers, tents, earthmoving/construction equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No personal monetary gain or unauthorized remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: No Army person or unit will realize a monetary profit or accept a gratuity or remuneration in any form not permitted by public law or Army regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize Armed Forces Day/Week community relations in May
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Armed Forces Day and Armed Forces Week observances to report the status of the Army to the Nation and demonstrate unity of the Armed Forces; see chapter 8 for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage acceptance of speaking invitations to inform public
rubrics_metrics.description: Army personnel are encouraged to accept speaking invitations at proper public events to inform the public of the Army’s mission and contribution to national security (see chapter 6 for more guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide orientation visits/open houses/briefings to satisfy public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum effort should be made to satisfy public interest via orientation visits and tours, periodic open houses, and briefing and discussion programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage ARNGUS and USAR community relations participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army National Guard (ARNGUS) and U.S. Army Reserve (USAR) organizations are encouraged to participate in community relations activities to the maximum extent possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider energy and environmental impact in planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Energy conservation and environmental impact issues will be prime considerations in planning and conducting community relations activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit association of community relations with vote soliciting
rubrics_metrics.description: Community relations activities cannot be associated with vote soliciting in any political election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraph 3–4 for election-year restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not participate in planned confrontational programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Army PA support of or participation in events where a public confrontation is planned or likely (or where the apparent purpose is to stage controversy) is unauthorized; participation is allowed where purpose is fair and equitable exchange of diverse opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership drives/fund‑raising endorsement restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, Army PA support will not officially endorse or appear to endorse membership drives or fund-raising activities for non-Federal entities; limited authorizations exist (CFC, approved emergency appeals, Army Emergency Relief, approved internal fund‑raisers) after consultation with ethics official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heads of ACOMs may authorize limited use of facilities/equipment for charitable events when they consider criteria identified in paragraph 3–2b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary private support to charities allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Army members may volunteer in their private capacity to charities of their choice, encouraged if they do not imply Department of the Army endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support requested by other Federal agencies not considered community relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Support requested by other Government agencies for official Government events (logistics, audiovisual, band, color guard) is not considered a community relations activity and is not subject to this regulation’s guidance; questionable official nature should be brought to OCPA attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD coordination for multi‑Service events
rubrics_metrics.description: OASD (PA) may appoint a DOD representative to coordinate military participation at certain public events when more than one Service is involved; when appointed, Army participation will be coordinated in advance through channels with the OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election‑year restrictions: avoid partisan association
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD/yearly PA guidance amplifies that DOD generally does not engage in activities that could be interpreted as association with partisan political causes, issues, or candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See detailed prohibitions below and consult DOD guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat political campaign worker inquiries as general public queries
rubrics_metrics.description: Inquiries from political campaign workers are considered queries from the general public and should be answered only with information/material available to the general public.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD PA broadcast/publication support for voting assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD PA broadcast activities and publications (AF and CE) will support the Federal Voting Assistance Program by carrying factual information about registration and voting laws (absentee voting requirements and key dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: AFRTS informational coverage rules
rubrics_metrics.description: AFRTS will broadcast balanced, nonfunded, informational coverage of political campaigns and elections from U.S. commercial/public networks free of charge; exercise care to provide news absent political comment, analysis, or interpretation; will not endorse or oppose candidates/causes and will not broadcast paid political ads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election‑year prohibitions on personnel and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel acting in official capacity may not engage in activities that associate DOD with any partisan political campaign, candidate, cause, or issue; requests for U.S. Army personnel to appear in/support political events will be denied; no personnel may wear military uniforms at campaign events (with limited exceptions for Joint Armed Forces Color Guards at formal party openings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No public commentary about political campaigns/elections without prior clearance from OASD (PA); no distribution of partisan literature by active duty personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on publishing campaign material or paid political ads
rubrics_metrics.description: PA programs, magazines, and publications will not publish information provided by a candidate’s campaign organization, partisan advertisements, editorials or commentaries dealing with political campaigns/elections, and CE newspapers/web sites partnered with Army may not carry paid political advertisements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No polls/surveys/straw votes on political campaigns in PA products
rubrics_metrics.description: No PA program, DOD newspaper, or CE endeavor may conduct or publish a poll, survey, or straw vote relating to political campaigns, elections, candidates, causes, or issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installations not to be used for campaign events
rubrics_metrics.description: Military installations will not be used by incumbents or candidates, their staff, or campaign representatives for campaign events (assemblies, town halls, polling, speeches, fund-raisers, press conferences, postelection celebrations); members of Congress may visit for official purposes but cannot engage in campaign activity during the visit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State facilities (e.g., armories) should follow applicable state law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media coverage of official visits by candidates restricted to official business
rubrics_metrics.description: When a candidate participates in official business, media may cover the event for official purposes, but under no circumstances may the candidate receive approval to make campaign or election-related statements or respond to campaign-related media queries during the official visit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny requests to film campaign commercials on military property
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to tape or film political campaign commercials in front of military equipment on Government-owned/leased property will be denied; does not apply to imagery taken outside installation confines or to elected officials on official business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria to establish Army PA publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders may establish Army PA publications only if: (1) a valid mission requirement exists; (2) the commander and ASCC/ACOM/DRU determine publication is the most effective means to fulfill/sustain the PA requirement; and (3) the ASCC/ACOM/DRU grants approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normally only one post publication authorized
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally only one post publication (newspaper or magazine) will be authorized at an installation, command, or community; commands supported by the installation publication are required to submit articles and assist with coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility study and CE publication rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders wishing to issue a publication will conduct a feasibility study with a civilian enterprise (CE). The commander or PA office provides oversight and final approval authority for news and editorial content. Detailed guidance in chapter 13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy exception requirements to issue more than one publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for a policy exception to issue more than one publication at an installation must be submitted through channels to the OCPA and must show audience dispersion or significantly different mission and include: commander’s requirement, publication mission statement, intended audience definition, PAO feasibility study for CE publication, format/name/frequency/reproduction/minimum editorial pages/color use/circulation/geographical area, and total editorial personnel required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using nonappropriated funds for AF and CE publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Using nonappropriated funds (NAFs) for Army Funded (AF) and CE publications is not authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See AR 215–1 for guidance on expending NAFs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriated funds not to pay civilian printer direct costs for CE
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriated funds may not be used to pay any part of a civilian printer’s direct costs to issue a CE publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major ACOM approval for non‑English CE publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Major ACOM approval is required for CE publications in languages other than English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial information products allowed with rights and fees met
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial information products may be used if all fees have been paid and copyright conditions have been met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on publicizing fund‑raising and games of chance
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicizing fund-raising activities, goals, quotas, or tallies is authorized only for CFC, Army Emergency Relief, and as provided elsewhere; publicizing games of chance has specific constraints (see paragraph 13–9g).

rubrics_metrics.name: CE newspaper contract and advertising restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: CE newspaper contracts will prohibit exclusive advertising agreements; CE publications are the only Army PA publications allowed to contain paid advertisements on a regular basis. AF publications will not contain commercial advertisements but may contain personal classified advertising at no cost to internal audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA office must approve news/editorial content of CE publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The news and editorial content of CE publications must be approved by the PA office. Publications and inserts become the property of the command/installation upon delivery according to contract terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain record copy of each PA publication issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Each PA office and post library will maintain a record copy (AR 25–400–2) of each issue of every publication produced under this regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish editorials (command position) vs commentaries (personal opinion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications will clearly identify editorials (command position) and commentaries (personal opinion) as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult SJA/provost marshal for legal notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Local Staff Judge Advocate and installation provost marshal should be consulted for guidance on placing legal notices required by Federal and state laws in Army PA publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory distribution and mailing requirements for PA publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for mandatory distribution: required mailing addresses and copy counts (SAPA–ZDA, AFIS, Defense Information School Journalism Dept, State Historical Society of Wisconsin, plus others as required by ACOM) and use of official mail/cheapest rates for ARNG/USAR newspapers; publications may also be placed in racks/stands in high-traffic areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on types of publications printed under this regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsletters, information bulletins, training publications, and similar publications (as defined by AR 25–30) will not be printed under the provisions of this regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To conserve resources, consolidate widely distributed bulletins into post newspaper when feasible.
